name: TruckTMS
tagline: Transport management software for road freight carriers: orders, trucks, drivers, trips, costs and invoicing in one place.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Strip a TMS down and most of it is relational CRUD: customers, trucks, trailers, drivers, loads, trips, expenses, invoices. An agent can produce that shape in a weekend and it will genuinely work for one small fleet that currently runs on spreadsheets. What it will not produce is the regulated edge: Romanian e-Factura submission to ANAF, SAF-T reporting, e-CMR, driver posting paperwork, tachograph and driving-hours tracking. It also will not produce the integrations that make a TMS sticky, freight exchanges like Timocom and Trans.eu, GPS telematics, fuel card imports, and the accountant's software. Build it if you want a dispatch board and a cost-per-kilometre number, not if you want the compliance machinery.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app where you enter loads, assign a truck and driver, log trip costs and kilometres, then generate invoices and a per-trip profitability view.
requirements: Node 20+ and a machine or small VPS to run it on
Somebody willing to keep entering data by hand
An accountant who will take CSV or PDF instead of a direct feed
whatYouLose: e-Factura / ANAF submission and SAF-T reporting, which are legal requirements, not features
Freight exchange integrations, so loads get retyped from Timocom or Trans.eu by hand
GPS telematics, so kilometres and positions are manual instead of pulled from the tracker
Driver hours, tachograph files and posting-of-workers paperwork
Mobile access for drivers, plus the small comforts: document expiry alerts, CMR scans, multi-currency fuel receipts
moatNotes: The CRUD is commodity. The Romanian fiscal plumbing and the freight exchange hookups are the part nobody wants to maintain alone.
whyPeopleStillPay: A carrier with twelve trucks is not buying a dispatch table, it is buying the guarantee that invoices land in ANAF the way the law currently requires, that the format changes get handled by somebody else, and that when a load is accepted on a freight exchange it does not need to be retyped at 11pm. The per-month cost is trivially less than one accountant hour per week, and the switching cost of moving years of trip and invoice history is what keeps anyone from leaving even when they grumble.
notes: Fine as a weekend dispatch board, dangerous as a replacement for anything a tax authority reads.
prompt:
Build a single-tenant transport management app for one small road freight carrier. No multi-tenancy, no signup flow.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js 15 App Router with TypeScript
- SQLite through better-sqlite3, file at ./data/tms.db, schema created by a migration script
- Tailwind for styling, no component library
- Zod for input validation
- pdf-lib for invoice and CMR-style PDF output
- Single shared password read from APP_PASSWORD in .env, checked by middleware, stored as an httpOnly cookie. Nothing else auth-related.

Data model: customers, trucks, trailers, drivers, loads, trips, expenses, invoices, invoice_lines, documents. A load has pickup and delivery addresses, dates, agreed price, currency and a reference. A trip assigns one truck, one trailer and one driver to one or more loads, and records start and end odometer.

Screens:
1. Dispatch board, loads grouped by status (new, assigned, in transit, delivered, invoiced), with drag-free status changes via a dropdown.
2. Trip detail: assigned loads, odometer, fuel and toll and other expenses, computed revenue, cost, margin and cost per kilometre.
3. Fleet and drivers lists with document expiry dates (insurance, ITP, licence, medical) and a dashboard panel listing anything expiring in the next 45 days.
4. Invoices: create from one or more delivered loads, sequential numbering with a configurable prefix, PDF export, mark as paid.
5. Reports: revenue and margin by month, by customer, by truck. CSV export on every table.

Explicitly out of scope, and say so in the README: e-Factura or ANAF submission, SAF-T, e-CMR, tachograph parsing, freight exchange integrations, GPS telematics, driver mobile app, email sending.

Ship a seed script with three trucks, four drivers and twenty loads so the screens are not empty. Write README.md covering setup, .env.example with APP_PASSWORD and INVOICE_PREFIX, and a one-line sqlite backup command. No telemetry, no external API calls, no cloud anything.
